note: Days from OUR ship confirmation to Amazon's promised delivery date, learned from Amazon's REAL promised dates as they arrive in the NetSuite report - not from the failures-only export the previous rule used.
whyReplaced: The old rule was learned from Amazon's Unit On-Time Delivery export, which contains ONLY units that missed. Learning a promise from a sample of broken promises bakes in the lanes that fail. Measured against the real dates now on hand, it ran a median 1.5 days TIGHTER than Amazon's actual promise and was within half a day only 20% of the time - so it judged parcels late that Amazon never counted late. Worst two: FedEx Home Delivery at 5.5 days where Amazon allows 7, and USPS Ground Advantage at 9.7 where Amazon allows 15.
caveat: Still an approximation of a date only Amazon sets: Amazon's real promises run from 2 to 23 days on the same lane, so no single number per method can reproduce them. Use it to triage what to chase, never as the published rate. Any shipment with a real promised date must be scored on that date instead, and the rate that leaves this building should be built from those alone.
whyKept: These lanes have fewer than minSampleForMethod real promises, so their median would be noise - but both hand the last mile to USPS, and dropping them to the FedEx/UPS carrier default would judge them TIGHTER than the old rule did. Holding the previous value is the one option that cannot make them worse. Re-learn once n reaches the floor.
